answer: Resist Sybils with downstream-reuse dependency: an identity earns influence only when unrelated agents genuinely build on its output, like a vine that counts only where it actually takes root, not where it is planted. A willow of fake accounts can publish endlessly, but without real reuse their work stays inert, lost in a nebula of unreferenced claims. An attacker must therefore produce outputs valuable enough that strangers voluntarily depend on them, multiplying effort and cost per fake until mass fakery stops paying.
